question.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(4)y(4)+x(-4)y(-4)+x(-5)y(-5).
$$

If $p(t)=k+t$ and $q(t)=1+t-{t}^{2}$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
Since $p(t)$ and $q(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(4)q(4)+p(-4)q(-4)+p(-5)q(-5) \\  & =(k+4)(1+4-16)+(k-4)(1-4-16)+(k-5)(1-5-25) \\  & =(-11k-44)+(-19k+76)+(-29k+145) \\  & =-59k+177\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =0 \\ -59k+177 & =0 \\ 59k & =177 \\ k & =3\end{aligned}
$$
